lines.text: I want to try two fixes for the race at once. One puts a lock around the queue, the other tries a different design. Do I fork?

lines.text: A fork is the tool for it, with one catch you should know first. A fork starts a second session from a copy of this one, up to a point. From there the two go their own ways, and the original is left as it was.

lines.text: So both forks know everything we've worked out so far.
Everything up to the fork point: what was read, the test that failed, the plan. That's the conversation, and the conversation is copied. Here's the catch: only the conversation is copied.

lines.text: Not the files. Both sessions still work on the same scheduler.py in the same folder. One rewrites the lock, the other rewrites it a different way, and each is changing the file under the other's feet.

lines.text: So it's a git branch, but for the chat.

Half right, and that's where it breaks. A git branch carries its own version of the files. A fork, on its own, is a new conversation over the very same files. For separate files you need a worktree: a second working copy of your repository, on a branch of its own, in another folder. A session working there can't touch your files.

lines.text: How do the three do it?
In Claude Code, /branch, or a fork option when you resume a session, copies the conversation into a new session. Only a worktree gives it its own files.

lines.text: /fork clones the chat and leaves the original untouched, either right here or in a new worktree. And pressing Escape twice edits your last message and forks from there.

lines.text: /fork copies the whole conversation, and Fork Conversation copies it up to a checkpoint, a saved copy of your files from before a request. A fork there doesn't get files of its own either.

lines.text: So for my two fixes: two forks, two worktrees.
Where your agent lets a fork have its own worktree, that's the safe version. Two conversations, two copies of the code, and your own folder left alone while they work.

Exactly. The conversation splits. The files only split if you split them.
